sources.title: Nintendo Switch Brew: Splay Applet

Lists the applet's IPC client services and notes that with 23.0.0+ the S1 applet gained news:c, stpl:sys, and FS permission bit47.

sources.title: TwistedVoxel: Nintendo Removes SmileBASIC 4 From UK eShop Amid News Of Switch 2 Jailbreak
sources.snapshot: Published 2026-10-22. Reports that the UK eShop delisted SmileBASIC 4 after the ns2jb release, that the game remained listed in the US, Canada, and Mexico at the time of writing, and summarises the two-bug chain (SmileBASIC array integer overflow, filesystem path-normalization buffer overflow).
sources.license: News reporting; cited as secondary reporting.
sources.notes: Delisting status is time-sensitive and region-dependent. Treat store availability as volatile.

sources.title: TwistedVoxel: Nintendo Switch 2 Jailbreak Exploits Expand Beyond SmileBASIC 4, Developer Claims
sources.snapshot: Published 2026-10-23. Reports that Gezine said SmileBASIC 4 is not strictly necessary, naming Artemis Engine and an undisclosed physical game cartridge as alternate methods, and that Gezine advised against buying Artemis Engine for this purpose because save-based exploits could stop working if online services are blocked.
sources.license: News reporting; cited as secondary reporting.
sources.notes: Secondary reporting of social-media claims. No technical details, package, or reproduction is provided.

sources.title: Wccftech: Nintendo Doubles Down on Switch 2 Security, But Developer Gezine Cracks a Universal Exploit That Works Entirely Offline
sources.snapshot: Published 2026-07-20. Quotes Gezine saying he created a Switch 1/2 userland exploit that is not a WebKit or save exploit, that it works offline and across all firmware versions, and that it is not a full jailbreak by itself.
sources.license: News reporting; cited as secondary reporting.
sources.notes: The claim is attributed to the developer's social-media posts. No code, advisory, or technical write-up was found.

sources.title: Ars Technica: Switch 2 security takes a hit as hackers unlock homebrew access
sources.snapshot: Published 2026-10-22. Reports that ns2jb gains userland access, that it requires a macOS or Linux PC on the same network running a Node.js package, that the entry bug is a 32-bit integer overflow when removing array items in SmileBASIC, and that the exploit falls well short of kernel-level access.
sources.license: News reporting; cited as secondary reporting.
sources.notes: Independent coverage corroborating the userland-only capability boundary.

sources.title: TechSpot: Nintendo Switch 2 jailbreaking is here, with homebrew, modding, and reverse engineering

sources.title: NVD: CVE-2023-4863
sources.snapshot: Describes a heap buffer overflow in libwebp's Huffman table construction, reachable through a crafted WebP image, fixed in libwebp 1.3.2 and exploited in the wild.
sources.license: Public vulnerability record; cited as an advisory.
sources.notes: A non-JIT image decoder bug, relevant to an engine that predates the September 2023 fix.

sources.title: The WebP 0day
sources.snapshot: Technical analysis of CVE-2023-4863: a heap buffer overflow in libwebp's BuildHuffmanTable reached through a crafted lossless WebP. Describes the trigger construction and reproduces it with AddressSanitizer against libwebp commit 7ba44f80f3b94fc0138db159afea770ef06532a0.
sources.license: Public technical write-up; cited as research literature.
sources.notes: Establishes the trigger conditions and the ASAN-based validation method.

sources.title: mistymntncop/CVE-2023-4863
sources.snapshot: Contains the craft harness, tree-visualisation tool, and two small reproducer files, bad.webp (236 bytes) and nso.webp (350 bytes). The README states 'A POC for CVE-2023-4863. NOT an exploit.'
sources.license: Public proof-of-concept repository; cited as a test corpus.
sources.notes: Used locally to validate the trigger. The reproducer files are not committed to this repository.

sources.title: Nintendo Support: Error Code 2802-9998
sources.snapshot: States that error 2802-9998 may occur when a captured video file has become corrupted, or when trying to view an unsupported video file on Nintendo Switch.
sources.license: Nintendo support documentation; quoted as vendor documentation.
sources.notes: Indicates that the 2802-xxxx family covers Album media access errors. The observed code 2802-9999 is a sibling.

sources.title: Nintendo Switch Brew: LDN services
sources.snapshot: Documents the ldn:m, ldn:s, and ldn:u services; security modes 1 (product, encrypted), 2 (debug), and 3 (system debug, plaintext); the authentication challenge added in 6.0.0; and the WLAN action-frame protocol.
sources.license: Community wiki; cited as protocol documentation.
sources.notes: The service-level reference for LDN. It establishes that retail uses security mode 1 and that plaintext modes are development-oriented.

sources.title: LDN Protocol (NintendoClients wiki)
sources.snapshot: Describes the LDN advertisement, authentication, and disconnect frames; the WLAN channels; AES-CTR and AES-GCM modes; and the authentication challenge that is always enabled for games but not for system titles.
sources.license: Community protocol documentation; cited as a reference.
sources.notes: The clearest public description of the frame layout and the challenge gate. It is a reverse-engineering reference, not a vendor specification.

sources.title: kinnay/LDN: Python package for local wireless communication with a Nintendo Switch
sources.snapshot: A Linux-only Python implementation that scans, joins, and hosts LDN networks. It requires monitor-mode action-frame support and CAP_NET_ADMIN/CAP_NET_RAW; retail encrypted networks require prod.keys. The source supports security mode 3 (system debug), where create_network does not derive a WLAN data key. Its host beacon uses SSIDElement("\x00" * 32); the network ID is carried in vendor action frames, not in the beacon SSID. The README confirms MediaTek/Realtek drivers and mt7921e.
sources.license: GPL-3.0; cited as a research tool, not vendored.
sources.notes: The practical host for the no-key plaintext test. It is not a game-sharing tool and does not bypass the ticket challenge.

sources.title: Nintendo Support: Virtual Game Card Guide
sources.snapshot: States that virtual game cards are linked to a Nintendo Account, that up to two consoles can load them, that both consoles must be connected to the internet, that local-wireless proximity is required for pairing and lending, and that lending is limited to Nintendo Account family group members.
sources.license: Nintendo support documentation; quoted as vendor documentation.
sources.notes: Establishes the account, internet, proximity, and license gates for the virtual-game-card path.

sources.title: Improve the 8822bu rtw88 in-kernel driver. Need testers...
sources.snapshot: A community testing thread for the in-kernel rtw88_8822bu driver. Participants report 'failed to get tx report from firmware' and beacon transmission failures in AP mode.
sources.license: GitHub issue content; cited as a community report, not as authoritative documentation.
sources.notes: Supports the interpretation that the Phase 2 host may not have transmitted. It does not prove that monitor-mode TX is impossible.

sources.title: Nintendo Switch Brew: NCA
sources.snapshot: Documents the NCA header layout, AES-XTS header encryption with a non-standard tweak, content types, key-generation fields, FsEntry and FsHeader structures, and the PartitionFS section format.
sources.license: Community wiki; cited as format documentation.
sources.notes: Used for read-only NCA header parsing. It does not provide keys or firmware.

sources.title: Linux mac80211 management-frame TX path
sources.snapshot: Reviewed ieee80211_mgmt_tx, ieee80211_mgmt_tx_skb, cfg80211_mgmt_tx_check, and the nl80211 FRAME_NO_STA attribute on 2026-10-29.
sources.license: GPL-2.0; cited as implementation documentation.
sources.notes: AP interfaces can send beacon frames through NL80211_CMD_FRAME. Non-public action frames require a station entry; FRAME_NO_STA does not bypass that check.

sources.title: Nintendo Switch Brew: WLAN services
sources.snapshot: Documents the wlan:inf, wlan:lcl, wlan:lg, wlan:lga, wlan:sg, wlan:soc, wlan:dtc, wlan, and wlan:p services, including Scan, Connect, CreateBss, PutActionFrame, GetActionFrame, and the 23.0.0 Scan struct size change.
sources.license: Community wiki; cited as service documentation.
sources.notes: Used to scope the general Wi-Fi management-frame surface. It describes the service API, not a vulnerability or a parser implementation.

sources.title: Nintendo Switch Brew: Sockets services
sources.snapshot: Documents bsd:u/bsd:s/bsd:a, bsdcfg/ifcfg, sfdnsres, nsd:u/nsd:a, and bsd:nu. It describes the FreeBSD-derived socket stack, the AddrInfo serialization format, and the 23.0.0 command additions.
sources.license: Community wiki; cited as service documentation.
sources.notes: Used to scope DHCP, DNS, and socket-service parsing. The 23.0.0 changelog separately records an AddrInfo deserialization fix.

sources.title: Nintendo Switch Brew: SSL services
sources.snapshot: Documents ssl and ssl:s, the NSS-backed client TLS implementation, ISslContext/ISslConnection commands, certificate import and verification options, and the 23.0.0 certificate-store update.
sources.license: Community wiki; cited as service documentation.
sources.notes: Used to scope the TLS handshake and certificate surface. It does not document a vulnerability.

sources.title: NVD: CVE-2023-28205
sources.snapshot: NVD record published 2023-04-10; CWE-416 use-after-free; CVSS 3.1 base 8.8; CISA KEV entry. Fixed in Safari 16.4.1, iOS 15.7.5 and 16.4.1, iPadOS 15.7.5 and 16.4.1, and macOS Ventura 13.3.1.
sources.license: NVD public data; cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: Used to identify the top no-JIT candidate. NVD does not publish the vulnerable function; the public PoC and the WebKit commit provide the structured-clone detail.

sources.title: About the security content of iOS 16.4.1 and iPadOS 16.4.1

sources.license: Apple advisory; cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: Confirms the fixed versions and the vendor's active-exploitation statement.

sources.title: WebKit commit c9880de: use MarkedVector in CloneDeserializer
sources.snapshot: Public WebKit commit referenced by the CVE-2023-28205 PoC. Not built or independently verified in this project.
sources.license: WebKit source is LGPL/BSD; the commit is cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: The PoC states that the fix replaces non-GC-scanned Vector containers with MarkedVector in SerializedScriptValue/CloneDeserializer.

sources.title: seregonwar/uaf-2023-28205: CVE-2023-28205 PoC
sources.snapshot: MIT-licensed PoC. README, index.html, and poc.js retrieved 2026-10-30. Targets WebKit-613.1.17.1; uses postMessage with Map/Date objects; crash analysis is from a PlayStation WebKit process, not the Switch.
sources.license: MIT License, Copyright (c) 2024 Nathan Fargo.
sources.notes: A public PoC is not evidence that the Switch build is vulnerable. Do not serve it without the W2 approval.

sources.title: WebKit Bugzilla 243557 (CVE-2022-32893)
sources.snapshot: Bug referenced by Apple's Safari 15.6.1 advisory and the oss-security discussion. The reviewed text does not identify the vulnerable component or a public PoC.
sources.license: WebKit Bugzilla; cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: CVE-2022-32893 is an out-of-bounds write fixed in Safari 15.6.1. It remains a secondary candidate only because the target build predates the fix.

sources.title: WebKitGTK and WPE WebKit Security Advisory WSA-2022-0009
sources.snapshot: Advisory dated 2022-09-19 covering CVE-2022-32912. Notes that the issue only affects macOS builds and credits the WebGL2 drawRangeElements analysis.
sources.license: Advisory; cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: CVE-2022-32912 is a WebGL2 bug; the console reports no WebGL, so it is excluded.

sources.title: NVD: CVE-2025-31200
sources.snapshot: CoreAudio APAC decoder memory corruption fixed in iOS 18.4.1, iPadOS 18.4.1, macOS Sequoia 15.4.1, tvOS 18.4.1, visionOS 2.4.1, and watchOS 11.5. CISA KEV.
sources.license: NVD public data; cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: Not a WebKit bug. The APAC codec is not expected on the Switch, so it is excluded from the browser candidate set.

sources.title: ns2jb run.cjs host entrypoint
sources.snapshot: Host entrypoint retrieved 2026-10-31. It hardcodes the Switch 2 target and spawns engine/switch2/pipeline.cjs.
sources.license: No license stated in the retrieved file; cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: Sets platform 2 and target 'switch2', copies engine/shared and engine/switch2 into the run folder, and spawns switch2/pipeline.cjs. There is no Switch 1 branch, so running it against a Switch 1 would not select a Switch 1 code path.

sources.title: ns2jb bootstrap.bas
sources.snapshot: SmileBASIC bootstrap retrieved 2026-10-31. It is labelled 'Switch 2 / SmileBASIC 4.4.9' and validates Switch 2 offsets and hashes.
sources.license: No license stated in the retrieved file; cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: Contains Switch 2-specific values such as &H9DB49C, &H5872F0, and &H12F614. A Switch 1 port would need different offsets, heap grooming, and a payload.

sources.title: What is ns2jb? The Switch 2 jailbreak situation explained
sources.snapshot: Article dated 2026-10-24, retrieved 2026-10-31. Timeline, capability table, eShop delisting, and unconfirmed brick reports.
sources.license: News article; cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: Confirms no CFW, no kernel exploit, no persistence, and that SmileBASIC 4.4.9 was required and then pulled from the eShop. Reports of consoles stalling at step 2/4 are unconfirmed. Notes that another entry point reaching fs may work, which is a claim, not a released method.

sources.title: Switch 2 Jailbreak Ported to WebKit by pepsipu
sources.snapshot: Article updated 2026-10-24, retrieved 2026-10-31. Reports a Discord claim that the port works on the author's Switch 2 and that testers were wanted for firmware before 23.0.1.
sources.license: News article; cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: States that no public download or full write-up had been posted. The claim is Switch 2-specific and does not describe a Switch 1 WebKit chain.

sources.title: cpypwn/mac2jb: an all-in-one ns2 jailbreaking tool for Mac
sources.snapshot: README retrieved 2026-10-31 (v0.6.0). MIT licensed. Requires an Apple Silicon Mac, a Switch 2 on 23.0.1, SmileBASIC full 4.4.9 or demo 4.4.6, Ethernet on the console, and an unsigned kernel extension with SIP disabled.
sources.license: MIT License.
sources.notes: Wraps ns2jb with USB keyboard automation and a MintBrew homebrew launcher. Switch 2 only. The unsigned USB gadget driver requires Reduced Security and csrutil disable, a system-wide macOS security change outside this project's authorization.

sources.title: kurumuz/ns2jb: Switch 2 FS demo fork
sources.snapshot: README retrieved 2026-10-31. Adds SmileBASIC 4.4.6 demo support, microSD Express layout handling, held RPC, and a system-code dump command.
sources.license: No license stated in the retrieved README; cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: Still 'Switch 2 only'. Requires Ethernet on both the PC and the console and warns that the FS exploit is very unstable, with at best about a 20% success rate.

sources.title: BermTheSequel/ns2jb2: Switch 2 FS demo fork
sources.snapshot: README retrieved 2026-10-31. Adds SmileBASIC 4.4.6 demo support and macOS, Linux, and Windows hosts.
sources.license: No license stated in the retrieved README; cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: Still a Switch 2 FS demo. Requires Ethernet and warns that the exploit is very timing-sensitive.

sources.title: DialingSpoon527/seedsow-lua-editor: Seedsow Lua Editor
sources.snapshot: README and installation guide retrieved 2026-10-31. 0BSD. Tested with US Seedsow Lullaby demo 1.0.0 on Switch 1 and Switch 2; the editor save is installed with JKSV on a hacked Switch 1 and transferred with Nintendo's official save transfer.
sources.license: 0BSD for project-owned code and documentation; game content retains its own rights.
sources.notes: The README calls the editor a foothold, not a full exploit. It requires a hacked Switch 1 seed and current firmware on both consoles for the official transfer. It does not provide fs-level code execution.

sources.title: ns2-savekit: Results
sources.snapshot: Hardware results on a retail Switch 2 with the Seedsow Lullaby demo/full. Reports full unsandboxed Lua 5.1 with io, os, debug, package, loadstring, and dofile; os.execute returns 0, io.popen is unsupported, sd: is absent, and save:/../ traversal is normalized away.
sources.license: Project documentation; cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: The Lua primitive is game-level save/VFS access, not fs-level. The fs sysmodule exploit is untested through this path.

sources.title: Seedsow Lullaby Opens New Switch 2 Homebrew Entry Point
sources.snapshot: Article updated 2026-10-30. Reports a save vulnerability in Seedsow Lullaby (Artemis engine), a free demo, a hacked Switch 1 seed, official save transfer, and an FS bootstrap still being written.
sources.license: News article; cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: States that the FS sysmodule exploit is still untested through this path and the bootstrap is not public. Both consoles need current firmware for the official transfer.

sources.title: Transferring users and save data
sources.snapshot: Official support page: you must update to the latest system version before carrying out a transfer; Data Management > Transfer Your Save Data.
sources.license: Nintendo support; cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: Used to assess the 22.0.0 seed versus the 23.0.1 OLED. It does not provide a save-signature bypass.

sources.title: NAX0 - Nintendo Switch Brew
sources.snapshot: Documents the AES-XTS NAX0 format used for SD-card files, the console-unique SD seed from ns_appman:/private, the sd_card_nca_key_source derivation, and the path-specific HMAC.
sources.license: Wiki; cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: Used to interpret the SD-card NCA containers read-only. It does not provide keys.

sources.title: How do you get your sd card encryption seed?
sources.snapshot: Forum guide: match the 16-byte Nintendo/Contents/private value in system save 8000000000000043 and take the next 16 bytes as the SD seed.
sources.license: Forum guide; cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: Community guide, not authoritative. Used only to explain why the card's private file is not the seed.

sources.title: Gezine entdeckt Userland-Exploit für Nintendo Switch 1 & 2
sources.snapshot: Published 2026-07-11. Reports an ARM64 ROP-based userland exploit for Switch 1 and Switch 2, offline, without WebKit or save data. Quotes Gezine's correction that 20.0.0+ firmware is needed on Switch 2 to enable Switch 1 compatibility, and that a physical cartridge with 20.0.0 firmware is needed to update manually.
sources.license: News article; cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: Used to correct the firmware-floor claim: 20.0.0+ applies to Switch 2's Switch 1 compatibility mode, not to Switch 1 itself.

sources.title: Gezine says there is a physical-cartridge exploit
sources.snapshot: Published 2026-10-22 and labelled rumor/unconfirmed. Reports Gezine saying SmileBASIC 4 is not strictly needed, that an exploit is based on a physical game cartridge, and that an untethered jailbreak may be possible. States none of it is released.
sources.license: Independent news site; cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: Used only to record the October claims and their unconfirmed status.

sources.title: Nintendo Switch 2's First Jailbreak Already Has YouTube Running on the Console, and an Untethered Exploit Is Reportedly Next
sources.snapshot: Published 2026-10-26. Reports a Gezine untethered concept for Switch 2: an installer that plants the exploit chain in save data and triggers on the next boot, providing userland-level access. Does not describe a Switch 1 package or a public release.
sources.license: News article; cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: Used to distinguish the Switch 2 untethered concept from the July Switch 1/2 userland claim.

sources.title: Gezine/CivSwitch: CivSwitch 1.0
sources.snapshot: README, repository tree, and release 1.0 (2026-11-01) retrieved 2026-11-03. MIT. XSS toolchain for the Switch 1 edition of Civilization VII; only the 1.0.0 physical cartridge is supported. Claims Switch 1/2 firmware 20.x.x through 23.0.1; tested on Switch 1 22.5.0 and Switch 2 20.4.0/23.0.1. Includes PicoSwitch (RP2040/RP2350 USB HID), core.js (V8 exploit and ROP), send_js.py, and installer-creator.
sources.license: MIT for project code; game content retains its own rights.
sources.notes: Used to record L-008/EP-012. The public code is stage 1 only; it contains no fs sysmodule payload. Switch 1 23.0.1 is claimed but not tested.

sources.title: CivSwitch core.js: chat XSS to V8 read/write and native ROP
sources.snapshot: 60,695-byte JavaScript payload retrieved 2026-11-03. Uses V8 pointer compression, addrof/fakeobj, arbitrary read/write, a ROP chain with game main-image and SDK gadgets, call_rop, and nn::socket functions; starts a TCP JavaScript loader on port 9026. No fs IPC or fs sysmodule payload.
sources.license: MIT for project code.
sources.notes: Read-only inspection. The ROP offsets are for the Civ VII 1.0.0 game build, not for a system sysmodule.

sources.title: CivSwitch PicoSwitch (Macro build)
sources.snapshot: RP2040/RP2350 firmware that acts as a Switch gamepad and USB keyboard macro and types the Civ VII chat-XSS payload once, about 10 s after boot. The shipped payload is the Remote JS Loader bootstrap, about 87 typed lines and about 15-20 minutes. Build presets are pico1 and pico2.
sources.license: MIT for project code.
sources.notes: The Pico is an external USB HID device, not a console modification. The README says the chat eval context is synchronous and the payload must not use top-level await.

sources.title: CivSwitch installer-creator
sources.snapshot: Installer that uploads a save template to the Remote JS Loader, splices a compressed payload into the currentTurnDate record, wipes every file in save:/saves/Single/, writes save:/saves/Single/XSTRIG.Civ7Save, and commits. Optional boot-persistent trigger; not needed for a session-only loader test.
sources.license: MIT for project code.
sources.notes: Destructive to Civilization VII save data. Do not run without a separate approval and a backup.

sources.title: CivSwitch offers a new offline entrypoint for Switch 2 homebrew
sources.snapshot: Published 2026-11-01. Reports Gezine's CivSwitch release, quotes the README's physical 1.0.0 cartridge requirement and Pico installer, and notes the game was readily available in the UK for about £30 at publication.
sources.license: News article; cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: Used for release date, public reception, and the approximate used-cartridge price. The article frames the release for Switch 2 homebrew, but the quoted README is for the Switch 1 edition.
